Succinct

/suhk-SINKT/ - the stress falls on SINKT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Succinct means marked by compact precision.

Field manuals prize succinct writing: every word a soldier reads in the rain has to earn its ink.

Worked Example

The winning grant application was four paragraphs in a stack of forty-page binders. The reviewers called it succinct, not thin: aims, method, budget, and proof of need were all there, each in exactly the sentences it required and not one more. Two committee members read it aloud in full, just because they could.

Succinct is the compliment here because it means marked by compact precision — everything needed, nothing extra, edges clean. Brief only counts the words; a rejection can be brief. And when shortness turns cold, you've crossed into this unit's terse — succinct never chills, it just doesn't waste.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

compact: much in little space — as true of cars as of prose

crisp: brisk and clean, with a snap of energy in it

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

long-winded: carrying on well past the point

padded: bulked with filler that adds nothing

Where it sits · how hard the wording is compressed — brief → succinct → telegraphic

brief vs. succinct: Brief is the bare stopwatch fact — short, with no promise that anything important survived the cut.

telegraphic vs. succinct: Telegraphic goes further than succinct — words drop out entirely, style pared to stubs, and completeness starts paying the bill.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — suc-

Prefix — suc-: under (a form of sub-)

Root — cinct

Root — cinct: girded, belted (Latin cingere)

Put it together

Put it together: Suc- (under) + cinct (belted) = 'girded up from under.' A Roman worker hitched his loose tunic up under his belt — succinctus — so nothing flapped or snagged. Succinct speech is dressed the same way: everything gathered in tight, nothing trailing.

Use the root in a new word: precinct

Use the root in a new word: precinct: A precinct is the district 'belted in' by a boundary line — the same cinct doing municipal duty.

Word Choice

neutral / admiring

Succinct is praise: compact and complete. Its neighbor terse — this unit — is shortness with a chill on it; brief is neutral arithmetic. Call a memo succinct and its author smiles; call it terse and they check their tone.
